blogs.title: Why Attention Slows Down Large Language Models – A Simple Explanation
blogs.description: An introductory post that walks readers through what the attention mechanism is, why it becomes a computational bottleneck as models grow, and how this limits long‑context applications such as reading whole documents or codebases.

blogs.title: From FlashAttention‑2 to FlashAttention‑3: Making GPUs Work Harder
blogs.description: A narrative of how FlashAttention‑2 improved attention speed but left most of the H100 GPU idle, followed by an explanation of the three new ideas in FlashAttention‑3 that raise utilization from ~35 % to ~75 %.

blogs.title: Producer‑Consumer Asynchrony & Warp‑Specialization: Turning Latency into Parallelism
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into the first key technique of FlashAttention‑3—splitting warps into producer and consumer groups, using circular shared‑memory buffers, and overlapping data movement with computation to hide memory latency.

blogs.title: Ping‑Pong Scheduling: Overlapping Softmax with Matrix Multiplication
blogs.description: Explains how the second technique hides the low‑throughput softmax operation behind high‑throughput GEMM calls, describing the two‑stage pipeline that lets one warp compute softmax while another is busy in Tensor Core matmuls.

blogs.title: FP8 Low‑Precision Attention: Speed Without Sacrificing Accuracy
blogs.description: Breaks down the challenges of moving to FP8 (layout constraints, quantization error), and shows how block quantization and incoherent processing keep numerical error low while nearly doubling FLOP throughput.

blogs.title: What 1.2 PFLOPs on an H100 Means for Real‑World AI
blogs.description: Translates the performance numbers (1.5–2× speedup, up to 740 TFLOPs/s FP16 and ~1.2 PFLOPs/s FP8) into practical gains for LLM inference, training, and future long‑context use cases.

blogs.title: A Beginner’s Guide to Building Faster Transformers with FlashAttention‑3
blogs.description: (Tutorial style) Walks developers through integrating FlashAttention‑3 into PyTorch or Hugging Face pipelines, covering required hardware (Hopper GPUs), installation steps, and simple code examples.
